specs.aspecto: 9:16 (square 1:1 also counts as a Short; 16:9 does not)
specs.ideal_nota: Heuristic, not a YouTube figure. Keep under 60 s whenever the Short carries third-party music: a Short over 1 minute with any active Content ID claim is blocked worldwide until the claim is resolved. Go 60-180 s only with royalty-free or own music and a story that needs it.

safe_area.nota: unverified: YouTube publishes no organic Shorts safe zone; these are the most widely cited third-party template values (channel name, Subscribe, title at the bottom; like/dislike/comment/share/remix column on the right). Safe box 840x960 starting at (48, 288).

caption_limit.nota: unverified (standard YouTube video limits, not re-fetched this session). The title is what the Shorts feed shows; front-load the keyword in the first ~40 characters.

specs.cover: Choose a frame from the Short in the app (pencil icon at upload or Edit after posting). A custom uploaded thumbnail for Shorts was reported rolling out in 2025-2026 (desktop Studio, some accounts only): unverified, check Studio. Design one frame (usually the hook frame) that reads as a cover: subject large, 2-4 words of text inside the safe box.

algoritmo: Shorts and long-form have separate recommendation systems; engagement on one format does not boost the other (YouTube Q&A as reported by Search Engine Journal).

Since 31 March 2025 a public Shorts view counts on every start or replay, with no minimum watch time; the old metric survives as 'engaged views', which is what YouTube Partner Program revenue uses. Optimise for engaged views and retention, not the public counter.

Studio's 'Viewed vs. swiped away' is the hook diagnostic: the share of feed impressions where the viewer stayed instead of swiping. YouTube publishes no target value; third-party guides cite 70-80% (unverified, creator-reported).
Recommendations are personalised from viewer behaviour (watch history, likes/dislikes, satisfaction); YouTube says the system has no preference for a Shorts format (secondary sources).

Originality: in 2026 YouTube said it is updating Shorts recommendations to prioritise original content and reduce reach of content re-uploaded from other creators; aggregators will likely see less distribution.

Monetisation: since 15 July 2025 the YPP 'repetitious content' policy is called 'inauthentic content' and targets mass-produced or repetitive videos (e.g. slight variations, slideshows without narration or educational value). It can apply to a whole channel. A templated faceless series must vary script, visuals and argument from episode to episode.
estrategia: Hook in the first 1-2 seconds with a visual and a spoken line that agree; check Viewed vs. swiped away per episode and A/B the opening line on the next episode, not the topic.
Loop the ending: last line or image leads back into the first so replays happen naturally (replays now count as views).

Use the 'Related video' link to send viewers from the Short to a long-form deep dive; say it on screen ('full story linked above the title'). Expect modest click-through (third-party: a few hundred to ~10% of viewers).
Series with numbered titles ('Hidden details #7') and a playlist; YouTube's search and suggested surfaces reward topical consistency.
Title = searchable phrase + curiosity ('The skull hidden in The Ambassadors'). Description: 1-2 sentences with names, dates, museum, plus sources; 3 hashtags max.
Educational value matters for the inauthentic-content policy: narration, a real argument and sources per episode.
cta: Soft verbal CTA after the payoff, not before: 'Part 2 is in the related video.'
Subscribe ask tied to the series promise in the last 2 s: 'One hidden detail every week.'
Pinned comment with the source list and the two-option question.

hashtags_seo.titulo: Keyword phrase people would type (artist + artwork + hook word). Titles are indexed by YouTube search; Shorts appear in search results.
hashtags_seo.hashtags: 2-3 relevant hashtags (#arthistory, #<artist>); YouTube shows hashtags above the title. Avoid long lists. unverified: exact display/limit rules not re-checked this session.
hashtags_seo.descripcion: Names, dates, places and sources in plain text; also helps the educational value case.
hashtags_seo.subtitulos: Upload the SRT/VTT from the pipeline (voice timeline) for accessibility and search; burned-in captions remain for the feed.

musica: Shorts audio library: most songs usable for up to 90 s of a 3-minute Short (some capped at 60 or 30 s). YouTube Audio Library royalty-free tracks get no Content ID claim. Any active claim on a Short longer than 60 s blocks it globally until resolved (no channel penalty). For this pipeline: own/generated music (ACE-Step) or Audio Library; never commercial tracks above 60 s.

ia_disclosure.obligatorio: Disclose realistic content that is generated or meaningfully altered with AI: real people saying/doing things they did not, altered footage of real events or places, realistic scenes that did not happen, and music that is the main focus.
ia_disclosure.no_obligatorio: Clearly unrealistic/animated content, minor aesthetic edits, beauty filters, captions, upscaling, AI used for ideas, scripts or thumbnails.
ia_disclosure.como: YouTube Studio upload > 'Altered or synthetic content' / 'AI use' = Yes. Label appears in the expanded description, or in the player for photorealistic or AI-music content. YouTube may auto-label from C2PA metadata or its own GenAI tools.
ia_disclosure.consecuencias: Disclosing does not limit audience or monetisation (YouTube's statement). Consistently not disclosing can bring a forced label, content removal or YPP suspension.
ia_disclosure.para_esta_app: A photoreal generated presenter with a synthetic voice is a realistic person who did not exist: set AI use = Yes on every upload. The collage style alone would not require it, but the presenter does.

publicacion.cadencia: No official Shorts cadence. Heuristic for a series: 3-5 Shorts per week, same days, plus one long-form per week or fortnight if the channel has it. Consistency over volume (unverified; creator consensus).
publicacion.horas: No official best time. Use Studio > Audience > 'When your viewers are on YouTube' once the channel has data; until then publish 2-3 h before the local evening peak of the main audience (unverified heuristic).

adaptar_desde_master: Keep 9:16 1080x1920; export H.264 high bitrate (YouTube re-encodes).

Move burned-in subtitles and key text above y=1248 (bottom 672 px are covered by title/channel/Subscribe) and left of x=888 (right action column). The collage style's y_subtitulos=1400 sits inside that zone.
If music is not royalty-free or own, trim the master to under 60 s or swap the track.
Write a search-style title (not the TikTok caption).
Add the Related video link and the AI disclosure toggle.
Optional: a looping last frame that matches the first frame.
